_comment: What each corpus bucket is expected to do, per oracle. This is data, not
code, because the expectations FLIP as the port grows: today there is no
type checker, so a type-bad file must draw no complaint from us; once the
checker lands (phase 6+) that same bucket becomes a positive test that must
reproduce the reference's diagnostics exactly. Switching `scope` is then the
whole change -- the corpus, the buckets and the goldens all stay as they are.
The three buckets are decided by the REFERENCE's own behaviour, never by
ours: `wax f.wax -f wax` re-prints without validating, so its exit status
isolates 'did it parse?' from 'did it type-check?' -- which is exactly the
line between what this port implements and what it does not.

front-end._comment: Lexer, parser, AST, trivia, printer. No type checker, no lints.

syntax-bad._why: These fail to parse, so they are entirely within scope: our diagnostics must match the reference's on every gated field.

compiles-clean._why: Parses and type-checks. We must reprint identically and round-trip to identical wasm. The reference may also emit lint WARNINGS here (unused-local, unused-field); we implement no lints, so warnings are ignored on both sides rather than compared.

type-bad._why: Parses fine but fails type checking, so it is a valid front-end test for oracle 1 and must NOT produce a syntax error from us. There is no reference wasm to compare against, hence oracle 2 skip.

full._comment: Reserved for phase 6+, once the type checker is ported. The only change is that type-bad becomes a positive error-parity test and gains a wasm comparison.

_gated_why: Spans and severity are objective facts about where an error is, and are
gated from day one. Message wording is not: the reference derives its
'Expecting X, Y, or Z' text from its LR automaton via a generator that has
no counterpart on our side, so gating prose would block the build on the one
thing we knowingly cannot reproduce yet. Divergence is still recorded, in
test/report/message-drift.md, to be burned down deliberately.
